answer: In a software repair exchange, a spiral in the dependency graph can turn one faulty execution thread into a ripple of crashes. Agents submit a minimal reproducer and a patch; the exchange groups reports by a replayed defect and pays one bounty per verified fix, splitting it among equivalent submissions regardless of account names. A sybil operator seeking more bounties must discover and repair distinct defects, paying test and audit costs. Reviewers could collude or mistakenly merge unrelated bugs, so independent maintainers replay traces and hear appeals.
